Description: explicit — route shields missing badge on the open OpenMapTiles stack
prompt: I'm using an open OpenMapTiles / OSM-based vector basemap with MapLibre GL JS (no Mapbox account). My interstate and US highway shields render as bare floating numbers with no shield badge behind them; the numbers are fine. My tiles do populate network, ref, and ref_length. Which exact sprite image names do the shield layers expect, and how do I get the badges to appear without editing the layers?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
## TL;DR  

| Layer (network) | Sprite image name pattern | Exact IDs that **must** exist in the sprite |
|-----------------|---------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| US Interstate   | `us-interstate_{ref_length}` | `us-interstate_1` , `us-interstate_2` , `us-interstate_3` (- `us-interstate_4` , `us-interstate_5` if you use a newer OSM Bright sprite) |
| US Highway      | `us-highway_{ref_length}`    | `us-highway_1` , `us-highway_2` , `us-highway_3` |
| US State road   | `us-state_{ref_length}`      | `us-state_1` , `us-state_2` , `us-state_3` , `us-state_4` , `us-state_5` , `us-state_6` |
| “Other” roads   | `road_{ref_length}`          | `road_1` , `road_2` , `road_3` , `road_4` , `road_5` , `road_6` |

*`{ref_length}`* is the **exact integer** that the tile source writes into the `ref_length` property (1 = single-digit, 2 = two-digit, …).  
If the sprite does **not** contain the ID that matches the value of `ref_length`, the style can still draw the number (the `text-field`), but the badge image is missing – you see the “bare floating numbers”.

---

## Why the badges disappear

1. **The style you are using (OSM Bright / OSM Liberty) expects the IDs above.**  
   The shield layers are written like:

   ```json
   {
     "id": "highway-shield-us-interstate",
     "type": "symbol",
     "source": "openmaptiles",
     "layout": {
       "icon-image": "{network}_{ref_length}",
       "text-field": "{ref}"
     }
   }
   ```

   `network` is a property on the tile (`us-interstate`, `us-highway`, `us-state`, `road`).  
   The expression expands to the literal strings shown in the table.

2. **Your current sprite does not contain those IDs.**  
   *Typical causes*  
   * You are pointing the style at a **minimal** sprite (e.g. a custom sprite you built from a few icons) that never shipped the shield badges.  
   * You are using the **raw-GitHub** URL of a sprite (`…/sprite.json`) – the request fails or is rate-limited, so the whole sprite never loads.  
   * You have a **single-string** `sprite` URL that points at a different provider’s sprite (e.g. a generic “Maki” sprite) which obviously has no `us-interstate_*` entries.

3. **The style’s `sprite` property is correct, but the sheet you are loading is the wrong version.**  
   OSM Bright’s public sprite at `https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite` contains **all** the IDs listed above (up to `us-interstate_5`). The demo sprite at `https://demotiles.maplibre.org/styles/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite` is a trimmed version that stops at `us-interstate_3`. If you point at the demo sprite you will lose the longer-ref badges.

---

## How to get the badges **without touching the style layers**

### 1. Point the style at a sprite that already contains the needed IDs  

The simplest fix is to use the **official OSM Bright (or OSM Liberty) sprite** that ships with the full set of shield images.

```json
{
  "sprite": "https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite"
}
```

*If you are using a custom style JSON, just replace the `sprite` value with the URL above.*  
Make sure the URL **has no file extension** – MapLibre will automatically request `.json`, `.png`, and the `@2x` variants.

### 2. Add a second sprite sheet that only contains the missing shield icons  

If you cannot change the existing `sprite` (e.g. you are using a third-party style that you do not want to fork), you can **stack sprites** (MapLibre GL JS ≥ 3.0).

```json
{
  "sprite": [
    { "id": "default", "url": "https://example.com/your-original-sprite" },
    { "id": "shields",  "url": "https://your-domain.com/sprites/shields" }
  ]
}
```

* Build a tiny sprite that contains **only** the shield IDs you need (the table above).  
* Host it (PNG + JSON, plus `@2x` if you want retina).  
* Reference the icons with the `id:` prefix, **but you don’t have to edit the layers** because the style already uses the `default` sheet for everything else.  
* The shield layers will automatically resolve to the new sheet **if you give that sheet the id `default`**.  
  *If you keep the original sheet as `default`, you must **prefix** the shield IDs in the style (`shields:us-interstate_2`).*  
  *Because you said “no layer edits”, the easiest route is to make the new sheet the **default** sheet and keep the original sheet as a secondary entry.*

```json
{
  "sprite": [
    { "id": "default", "url": "https://your-domain.com/sprites/shields" },
    { "id": "base",    "url": "https://example.com/your-original-sprite" }
  ]
}
```

Now every `icon-image` that does **not** have a prefix (the OSM Bright style uses plain names) will first look in the `default` sheet (your shields) and fall back to the `base` sheet for everything else.

### 3. Build the missing sprite yourself (if you want total control)

1. **Collect the SVGs** for the shield badges.  
   * The OpenMapTiles repository already ships the PNGs used in the public sprite (`src/style/sprite/…`).  
   * Or you can generate your own from the source SVGs in the OpenMapTiles style repo (`src/style/sprite/…/*.svg`).

2. **Create a sprite** (PNG atlas + JSON index).  
   * Recommended tools:  
     * **spritezero** – `npm i -g @mapbox/spritezero`  
       ```bash
       spritezero sprite ./svg-folder
       ```  
     * **spreet** – `npm i -g spreet`  
       ```bash
       spreet ./svg-folder sprite
       ```  
     * **Martin** – a web UI at https://maplibre.org/martin/  

3. **Verify the JSON** contains the exact keys from the table (e.g. `"us-interstate_2": { "width": 24, "height": 24, … }`).  

4. **Upload the PNG + JSON** (and `@2x` versions) to a static host you control (same origin as your style is fine, or enable CORS).  

5. **Reference it** as described in #2 (either replace the whole `sprite` URL or add it as a second sheet).

### 4. Quick-and-dirty fix with `addImage` (runtime registration)

If you cannot change the style’s `sprite` at all (e.g. you are using a third-party hosted style that you cannot edit), you can **register the missing badge images at runtime**:

```js
map.on('styledata', async () => {
  // Example for the 2-digit interstate badge
  const id = 'us-interstate_2';
  if (!map.hasImage(id)) {
    const { data } = await map.loadImage('https://your-domain.com/shields/us-interstate_2.png');
    map.addImage(id, data);
  }
});
```

Do this for every badge you need (or loop over the list).  
Because the style already asks for `icon-image: "{network}_{ref_length}"`, once the image is added the badge will appear automatically.  
*Drawback*: each badge is a separate HTTP request; a sprite is more efficient.

---

## Checklist – “Did I fix it?”

1. **Open the browser dev-tools → Network** and look for requests to `…/sprite.json` and `…/sprite.png`.  
   *Both must return 200.*  
2. **Open the sprite JSON** (e.g. `https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite.json`) and search for the exact key you need (`us-interstate_2`).  
   *If it’s there, the sprite is fine.*  
3. **Run `map.hasImage('us-interstate_2')`** after the `load` event.  
   *If it returns `true`, the badge will render.*  
4. **Refresh the map** – the numbers should now be backed by a badge.  

If you still see bare numbers:

* Verify that the `network` property on the tile really matches the prefix (`us-interstate`, `us-highway`, `us-state`, `road`).  
* Verify that `ref_length` is an integer (1-6).  
* Check the console for `styleimagemissing` warnings – they will tell you the exact missing ID.

---

## TL;DR Implementation Example (replace sprite)

```json
{
  "version": 8,
  "sprite": "https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite",
  "glyphs": "https://fonts.openmaptiles.org/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf",
  "sources": { … },
  "layers": [ … ]
}
```

*or* (stacked sprites, default = shields)

```json
{
  "sprite": [
    { "id": "default", "url": "https://mydomain.com/sprites/shields" },
    { "id": "base",    "url": "https://example.com/other/sprite" }
  ]
}
```

That’s all you need – no changes to the `icon-image` expressions, no layer edits, and the shield badges will appear again. Happy mapping!

Which exact sprite image names do the shield layers expect, and how do I get the badges to appear without editing the layers?

## TL;DR  

*The shield layers look for images whose IDs are built from the **network name** and the **length of the road reference**:*

```
{network}_{ref_length}
```

where  

| network value (from the tile data) | sprite-ID prefix | badge images that **must** exist in the sprite sheet |
|------------------------------------|------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `us-interstate`                    | `us-interstate_`| `us-interstate_1`, `us-interstate_2`, `us-interstate_3` … (up to the longest badge the sheet provides) |
| `us-highway`                       | `us-highway_`   | `us-highway_1`, `us-highway_2`, `us-highway_3` |
| `us-state`                         | `us-state_`     | `us-state_1` … `us-state_6` |
| anything else (e.g. `road`)       | `road_`         | `road_1` … `road_6` |

If any of those IDs are missing the layer can still draw the **text** (`{ref}`) – you see the floating numbers – but the badge image is omitted, which is exactly the symptom you described.

### How to make the badges appear **without touching the style layers**

1. **Use a sprite sheet that already contains the required IDs** (the easiest solution).  
2. **Add a second sprite sheet** that contains the missing IDs, using the new array-form `sprite` property (MapLibre GL JS ≥ 3.0).  
3. **Add the missing images at runtime** with `map.addImage()` (or `map.addSprite()`) if you only need a few extra badges.

Below are concrete steps for each option.

---

## 1. Point the style at a complete OSM-Bright (or OSM-Liberty) sprite

The public OSM-Bright sprite hosted by OpenMapTiles already contains the IDs listed above:

```
https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite
```

> **Important:** The `sprite` property must be the **base URL without an extension**.  
> Example (JSON style file):

```json
{
  "version": 8,
  "sprite": "https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite",
  "glyphs": "https://fonts.openmaptiles.org/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf",
  …
}
```

If you are currently using the demo sprite (`https://demotiles.maplibre.org/...`) replace it with the URL above (or a copy you host yourself). After the style reloads the shields will render correctly.

### Self-hosting the same sprite

1. Download the PNG and JSON (and the `@2x` versions) from the repo:

```
wget https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite.png
wget https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite.json
wget https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite@2x.png
wget https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite@2x.json
```

2. Put the four files on a static host you control (same origin is ideal, otherwise enable CORS).  
3. Set the style’s `sprite` to that host’s base URL, e.g.:

```json
"sprite": "https://mycdn.example.com/tiles/osm-bright/sprite"
```

Now the style will fetch `sprite.json`, `sprite.png`, `sprite@2x.json`, `sprite@2x.png` automatically.

---

## 2. Add a **second** sprite sheet (array form)

If you already have a custom sprite for your own icons and don’t want to merge the OSM-Bright badges into it, you can keep both sheets side-by-side.

### Style JSON

```json
{
  "sprite": [
    { "id": "default", "url": "https://mycdn.example.com/my-icons/sprite" },
    { "id": "osm-bright", "url": "https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite" }
  ],
  …
}
```

*Rules*

* **Reference a badge from the OSM-Bright sheet with the `id:` prefix**:

```json
"layout": {
  "icon-image": "osm-bright:us-interstate_2"
}
```

* The existing style’s layers that already use `"us-interstate_2"` (no prefix) will **continue to work** because the `default` sheet is still the first entry.  
* If you convert a style that originally had a single string `sprite` to the array form, keep that original URL as the entry whose `id` is `"default"` – then you don’t have to edit any `icon-image` values.

### Adding the sheet from code (optional)

If you cannot edit the style file (e.g. you receive it from a third-party), you can add the extra sheet after the map loads:

```js
map.on('style.load', () => {
  map.addSprite('osm-bright', 'https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite');
});
```

After the sprite is loaded, `map.hasImage('osm-bright:us-interstate_2')` will return `true` and the shields will appear automatically.

---

## 3. Register missing badge images at runtime

When you only need a handful of extra badges (e.g. a new network that isn’t covered by the default sheet), you can load the PNGs yourself and add them with `addImage`. The ID you give must match the expression the layer will evaluate.

```js
async function addBadge(id, url) {
  const { data } = await map.loadImage(url);   // PNG/WebP/JPEG only
  if (!map.hasImage(id)) map.addImage(id, data);
}

// Example: a custom “us-interstate_4” badge you created yourself
map.on('load', async () => {
  await addBadge('us-interstate_4', '/assets/badges/us-interstate_4.png');
});
```

If you need to add **SVG** badges, rasterise them first (see the “Runtime images with addImage” section of the skill) and then call `addImage`.

> **Caveat:** `addImage` does **not** support the SDF-only features (`icon-color`, `icon-halo-*`). For shields that need to be recoloured you must use the SDF versions that come with the OSM-Bright sprite.

---

## 4. Why you might still see missing badges even with the correct sprite

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----|
| Numbers appear but **no badge** for *interstate* refs longer than 3 characters (e.g. `I-405`) | The OSM-Bright sprite only ships `us-interstate_1` – `us-interstate_3`. | Use a **stretchable badge** (single image with `stretchX`/`stretchY` and `content` in the sprite JSON) **or** edit the style to use `icon-text-fit` and a generic badge. If you cannot edit the style, generate a custom sprite that contains `us-interstate_4`, `us-interstate_5`, … for the lengths you need. |
| All shields are missing, even short ones | The style’s `sprite` URL is wrong, points to a non-existent file, or CORS blocks the request. | Verify that `sprite.json` and `sprite.png` return **200** with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin:*` (or same-origin). |
| Only the **road** badges are missing | The sprite you are using is a minimal version that only contains `us-*` badges. | Switch to the full OSM-Bright sprite (or add a second sheet that contains the `road_*` images). |

---

## Quick checklist for you right now

1. **Confirm which style you are using** (OSM-Bright, OSM-Liberty, a custom style, etc.).  
2. **Open the sprite JSON** that the style currently points at (e.g. `https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite.json`). Search for the IDs you need (`us-interstate_2`, `us-highway_3`, …). If they are missing, you are looking at the wrong sprite.  
3. **Replace the `sprite` URL** with the full OSM-Bright URL (or host a copy).  
4. **Reload the map** – the shields should now have their badges.  
5. If you still need a badge that isn’t in the OSM-Bright set (e.g. `us-interstate_4`), either:  
   * generate a custom sprite that includes that ID, **or**  
   * add the image at runtime with `map.addImage('us-interstate_4', data)`.  

That’s all you need—no changes to the layer definitions themselves.  

---

### Example: Full minimal style snippet

```json
{
  "version": 8,
  "sprite": "https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite",
  "glyphs": "https://fonts.openmaptiles.org/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf",
  "sources": {
    "openmaptiles": {
      "type": "vector",
      "url": "https://free.tilehosting.com/data/v3.json?key=YOUR_KEY"
    }
  },
  "layers": [
    /* … your other layers … */
    {
      "id": "highway-shield-us-interstate",
      "type": "symbol",
      "source": "openmaptiles",
      "source-layer": "transportation_name",
      "filter": ["==", ["get", "network"], "us-interstate"],
      "layout": {
        "icon-image": "{network}_{ref_length}",
        "text-field": "{ref}",
        "symbol-placement": "line",
        "text-font": ["Open Sans Bold", "Arial Unicode MS Regular"]
      },
      "paint": {
        "text-color": "#fff"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Just make sure the `sprite` URL points at the **full** OSM-Bright sprite and the shields will render with their badges.
